data.narrative:
GITAI, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $129M+, was valued using two triangulation methods against a peer set of 9 companies (1 public, 8 private) spanning robotics and adjacent automation sectors. The peer universe includes Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), among others.

Stage-progression analysis applied a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $129M capital raised proxy, implying a $219M valuation. Peer-median analysis of seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yielded a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. These two methods produce substantially divergent signals, reflecting the wide dispersion in robotics company valuations at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $186M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $935M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate multiples in an early-stage, capital-intensive sector where peer valuations cluster at $1.6B–$2.0B despite heterogeneous funding stages. The key tension is whether GITAI's position within the peer distribution warrants valuation closer to the stage-progression floor or to peer medians. Resolution requires assessment of relative technology maturity, commercial traction, and capital efficiency versus named comparables.
